method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited instruction address, operand, name literal, holder vftable cell, type descriptor name, RTTI name and call target was compared with those listings. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of the fourteen natives that run on the zone-in, fade, weather, music, notice and calendar paths: _waitForMapLoaded, _fadeInAfterWarp, _resetFade, _isFading, _cancelFading, _setWeather, _setMusic, _isEventPlaying, _cancelNotice, _readyInnBed, _getHydaelynTime, _getHydaelynMoon, _getHydaelynHour and _getAreaType. Each row gives the registration site, receiver type check, declared argument and return lists, reads, client state effects, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish fade, weather, music or notice presentation, calendar semantics or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

tierVocabulary.STATIC: Read directly from instructions or data at the cited addresses.
tierVocabulary.INFERRED: A name or role assigned from the surrounding instructions. The bytes do not state it.

framework.reference: manifests/fade_actor_group_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling, the holder receiver adapter, the world object chain and the yield request.

MyPlayer.note: The only class whose RTTI base list names PlayerBase. It registers nothing, since its slot 2 holds 0x00776340. The PlayerBase cell of a thunked native holds a bare ret 4 or 0x00776340, so a PlayerBase receiver that is not a MyPlayer pushes no value.

listBuilders.note: A builder selects registry entries through 0x00CCA210. Entry 0 is int, 1 float, 2 bool, 3 Utf8String and 4 LuaControl*.

worldObject.chain: R is the address that 0x00CC7510 returns for ExecuteParameters +0x04. X = [R], Y = [X +0x04] and W = [Y].

fields.W (Y +0x00): Object whose first dword is V. _setWeather, _setMusic and _waitForMapLoaded use it.
fields.Y +0x08: Object whose first dword is V. The fade natives use it.
fields.V +0x4CC: Fade object F, as in the fade contracts.
fields.V +0x4E0: Object whose byte +0xB9 gates _waitForMapLoaded and which receives the weather requests.
fields.V +0x928: Embedded object that receives the music control 0x004BBB30.
fields.V +0x17758: RaptureUserControl, vftable 0x00F90F64, four counters at +0x18, +0x2C, +0x40 and +0x54.

rows.callbackKind: thunk through a receiver vftable slot

arguments.note: Optional. A Nil cell skips the read. Any other cell is read as an int and the value is dropped, so it has no effect beyond the type check.

rows.behavior: Tail-jumps through slot 0x13C of the receiver vftable. The PlayerBase routine is a bare return. The MyPlayer routine skips a Nil cell and otherwise reads an int that it discards. It reads the byte at +0xB9 of the object at V +0x4E0. A zero byte returns at once. A nonzero byte builds a four byte s_MapLoadResumeChecker and requests a yield. The checker repeats the byte test and ends the wait when the byte is zero. It pushes no value.

facts.claim: The callback is the thunk 'mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0x13C]; jmp eax'. The PlayerBase vftable 0x00FD5E04 cell 0x00FD5F40 holds 0x006DEAB0, a bare 'ret 4'. The MyPlayer vftable 0x00FD785C cell 0x00FD7998 holds 0x006E5EB0.

The MyPlayer routine loads the tag byte of cell 0 at +0x0C and compares it with 6. A Nil cell jumps over the read. Any other cell is read through 0x005819A0 and the returned pointer is not used again.
The routine resolves the world chain, loads W and calls 0x0075C820. That routine loads V, calls 0x004D7390, which returns the dword at V +0x4E0, and returns the byte at +0xB9 of that object.

A zero byte jumps to the epilogue with no yield. A nonzero byte allocates four bytes through 0x009D1B35, constructs the checker with 0x00716530 and calls the yield request 0x00CD2860 with ExecuteParameters +0x08.

The checker is s_MapLoadResumeChecker (vftable 0x00FD5638). Its poll slot 0x0071C7F0 resolves the world chain, calls 0x0075C820 on W and stores the waiting result 0x0130CECC while the byte is nonzero and the done result 0x01377ECC once it is zero. Its push slot 0x00A72A20 is 'ret 0xC' and pushes nothing.

The byte at +0xB9 is a map load pending flag, by the native name. The class of the object at V +0x4E0 and the writers of the byte were not traced. The same object receives the weather requests of _setWeather.

rows.behavior: Tail-jumps through slot 0x100 of the receiver vftable. The PlayerBase routine is a bare return. The MyPlayer routine calls 0x0075B500, which runs 0x004D6FE0 with two zero arguments, then 0x0075B300, which adds 1 to all four RaptureUserControl counters, and stores 1 in the byte at MyPlayer +0x166. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback is the thunk 'mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0x100]; jmp eax'. The PlayerBase vftable 0x00FD5E04 cell 0x00FD5F04 holds 0x00776340, a bare 'ret 4'. The MyPlayer vftable 0x00FD785C cell 0x00FD795C holds 0x006E3260.
The MyPlayer routine resolves the world chain, loads the dword at Y +0x08 into ESI, calls 0x0075B500 and 0x0075B300 on it and stores 1 in the byte at the receiver +0x166.

0x0075B500 loads V and calls 0x004D6FE0 with two zero arguments. 0x004D6FE0 returns when the dword at V +0x175A4 is null. Otherwise it calls 0x0056A5F0 on the object at V +0x175A4 with the two arguments, calls virtual slot 0x38 of the object embedded at V +0xB4, calls 0x0091C230 with 0 and calls 0x004D6820 with 0.0, 0, 0 and 0. The effects of those calls were not traced.

0x0075B300 loads V, takes the RaptureUserControl at V +0x17758 through 0x004D7580 and calls its virtual slots 1, 4, 7 and 10. Those routines are 0x0054B440, 0x0054B620, 0x0054B650 and 0x0054B680 and add 1 to the player, target cursor, lock-on and camera counters at object +0x18, +0x2C, +0x40 and +0x54.
The byte at MyPlayer +0x166 records that the counters were raised here, because _resetFade tests it before it lowers them. Its other writers and readers were not traced.

rows.behavior: Tail-jumps through slot 0x104 of the receiver vftable. The PlayerBase routine is a bare return. The MyPlayer routine runs the zero frame fade in 0x0075B490, stores 0 in the byte at MyPlayer +0x165 and, when the byte at +0x166 is nonzero, calls 0x0075B510 and 0x0075B330 and clears the byte. 0x0075B330 subtracts 1 from all four RaptureUserControl counters. facts.claim: The callback is the thunk 'mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0x104]; jmp eax'. The PlayerBase vftable 0x00FD5E04 cell 0x00FD5F08 holds 0x00776340, a bare 'ret 4'. The MyPlayer vftable 0x00FD785C cell 0x00FD7960 holds 0x006E32A0.

The MyPlayer routine calls 0x0075B490 on the dword at Y +0x08 with the frame count 0. It then compares the byte at the receiver +0x166 with 0 and stores 0 in the byte at +0x165. A zero byte at +0x166 ends the routine.

A nonzero byte at +0x166 calls 0x0075B510 and 0x0075B330 on the same dword and stores 0 in the byte. 0x0075B510 runs 0x004D70B0 with the argument 1, the routine of _fadeInNowLoadingForNoticeEventJustInArea.
0x0075B490 loads V and F from V +0x4CC and calls 0x005606B0 with four 0.0 floats and the frame count, the fade in of _fadeIn. A frame count of 0 leaves the byte at F +0x244 clear.

0x0075B330 takes the RaptureUserControl through 0x004D7580 and calls its virtual slots 2, 5, 8 and 11. Those routines are 0x0054B600, 0x0054B630, 0x0054B660 and 0x0054B8C0 and add -1 to the counters at object +0x18, +0x2C, +0x40 and +0x54 with no floor test.

rows.callbackKind: thunk through a receiver vftable slot

arguments.note: Weather id. The routine keeps the low 16 bits (MOVZX) and the engine side sign-extends them from 16 bits.
Second value. The routine keeps the low 8 bits and the engine side sign-extends them from 8 bits.

rows.behavior: Tail-jumps through slot 0x144 of the receiver vftable. The PlayerBase routine is a bare return. The MyPlayer routine reads two ints, keeps the low 16 bits of the first and the low 8 bits of the second and calls 0x0075C910 with W. That routine sign-extends both and calls 0x0059E700 on the object at V +0x4E0. A nonzero weather id sends two scene records. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback is the thunk 'mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0x144]; jmp eax'. The PlayerBase vftable 0x00FD5E04 cell 0x00FD5F48 holds 0x00776340, a bare 'ret 4'. The MyPlayer vftable 0x00FD785C cell 0x00FD79A0 holds 0x006E6070.
The MyPlayer routine reads cell 0 through 0x005819A0 and keeps the word with MOVZX, reads cell 1 and keeps the low byte, resolves the world chain and calls 0x0075C910 on W with the word and the byte.
0x0075C910 loads V, takes the object from V +0x4E0 through 0x004D7390, sign-extends the word with MOVSX and the byte with MOVSX and jumps to 0x0059E700.
0x0059E700 builds a 16 byte record from the extended byte (dword 0), its sign (dword 1) and 0.0 (dword 2), leaves dword 3 unwritten and calls 0x0059E4D0 with the extended id and the record.

0x0059E4D0 does nothing for the id 0. For a nonzero id it calls 0x0059E1F0, which copies the record to object +0x128 and sends it as record number 0x72 with 0x10 bytes through 0x004D7980. It then stores the id at object +0x9C and sends it as record number 0x0C with 4 bytes. 0x004D7980 adds 0x15 to the record number, so the scene packet types are 0x87 and 0x21. The routine ends by storing 0 at +0xA0, +0xA4 and +0xB0 and the byte 0 at +0xBB, whatever the id.

The id is a weather number and the second value a transition or mode number, by the native name. Their ranges, the consumer of the two scene records and the class of the object at V +0x4E0 were not traced.

arguments.note: Event name. It is read only when the byte at MyPlayer +0x5C is nonzero.

returns.note: False when the byte at +0x5C is zero, otherwise the byte that 0x00894140 returns.

rows.behavior: Tail-jumps through slot 0xE0 of the receiver vftable. The PlayerBase routine is a bare return that pushes nothing. The MyPlayer routine pushes false when the byte at +0x5C is zero. Otherwise it reads a Utf8String and calls 0x00894140 on the object at MyPlayer +0xF8 with it, then pushes the returned byte through the bool pusher. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback is the thunk 'mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0xE0]; jmp eax'. The PlayerBase vftable 0x00FD5E04 cell 0x00FD5EE4 holds 0x006DE980, a bare 'ret 4'. The MyPlayer vftable 0x00FD785C cell 0x00FD793C holds 0x00704DB0.
The MyPlayer routine tests the byte at the receiver +0x5C first. A zero byte pushes a false byte through 0x00748870 and returns without reading the argument.
A nonzero byte reads cell 0 through 0x0071CE70, calls 0x00894140 with ECX set to the dword at the receiver +0xF8 and the string, and pushes the returned byte through 0x00748870.

0x00894140 takes P from this +0x08 and Q from P +0x04. When the virtual slot 0x18 call on Q with the constant 0x0134C3FF returns zero and the name at Q +0x04 compares equal through 0x00445D20, which returns 1 on a match, it returns whether the byte at P +0x21 is nonzero. Otherwise it walks the list whose sentinel pointer is at this +0x14 and returns 1 for the first node whose slot 0x18 call with the constant does not return 1 and whose name compares equal. The end of the list returns 0.

The object at MyPlayer +0xF8 is the event or notice queue of the player, by the paired _cancelNotice call on the same object. Its class, the meaning of the constant 0x0134C3FF and the writers of the entries were not traced.

arguments.note: Optional. A Nil cell selects the variant with no byte. Any other cell is read as an int and its low 8 bits are passed by pointer.

A Nil cell calls 0x00895060 on the object at MyPlayer +0xF8 with the receiver, the string and the constant 0x012C3F7E. Any other cell is read as an int and 0x008950D0 is called with the same three values and a pointer to the low byte of the int. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback is the thunk 'mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0xD0]; jmp eax'. The PlayerBase vftable 0x00FD5E04 cell 0x00FD5ED4 holds 0x006DE940, a bare 'ret 4'. The MyPlayer vftable 0x00FD785C cell 0x00FD792C holds 0x006E8F50.
The MyPlayer routine reads cell 0 through 0x0071CE70 and then compares the tag byte of cell 1, at cell +0x0C, with 6.
A Nil cell 1 calls 0x00895060 with ECX set to the dword at the receiver +0xF8 and the stack values receiver, string and 0x012C3F7E.

Any other cell 1 is read through 0x005819A0 and the low byte is stored on the stack. 0x008950D0 is called with ECX set to the dword at the receiver +0xF8 and the stack values receiver, string, 0x012C3F7E and the address of that byte.

0x00895060 releases the entry at this +0x0C, through its virtual slot 0 with the argument 1, when the name at its object +0x04 compares equal through 0x00445D20 and its virtual slot 0x18 call with the constant returns 1. It clears this +0x0C and then calls 0x00894800 and 0x008949A0 with the receiver, the string and the constant. 0x008950D0 adds a byte condition: the byte that 0x00892530 returns must not exceed the byte at the last argument, as an unsigned compare, before it releases the entry at this +0x0C or calls 0x00894800 for the entry at this +0x08. The meaning of 0x00892530 was not traced.

arguments.note: The bed or chara control. It is read only when the byte at MyPlayer +0x161 is nonzero.

returns.note: True when the byte at +0x161 is 0x15 or more as a signed value. Nil in the other two cases, even though the return list declares a bool.

rows.behavior: Tail-jumps through slot 0x1FC of the receiver vftable. The PlayerBase routine is a bare return. The MyPlayer routine pushes nil when the byte at MyPlayer +0x161 is zero. Otherwise it reads a chara, stores its identity at MyPlayer +0x130 and pushes nil when the byte at +0x161 is below 0x15 as a signed value or stores 0xE0000000 at +0x128 and pushes true. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback is the thunk 'mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0x1FC]; jmp eax'. The PlayerBase vftable 0x00FD5E04 cell 0x00FD6000 holds 0x00776340, a bare 'ret 4'. The MyPlayer vftable 0x00FD785C cell 0x00FD7A58 holds 0x00706700.
The MyPlayer routine tests the byte at the receiver +0x161. A zero byte jumps to the nil pusher 0x00748920 with the return cell vector at ExecuteParameters +0x1C and reads no argument.
A nonzero byte reads cell 0 through the chara cast reader 0x0071BC90, converts the control to an identity through 0x00CC73B0 and stores the identity at the receiver +0x130.

The routine then compares the byte at +0x161 with 0x15 using a signed jump. A smaller value pushes nil through 0x00748920. Otherwise it stores the dword at 0x0130C778, 0xE0000000, at the receiver +0x128 and pushes a true byte through 0x00748870.

The byte at +0x161 is a stage or state counter of the inn bed sequence, by the native name. Its writers and the readers of +0x128 and +0x130 were not traced. _fadeInNowLoadingForNoticeEventJustInArea tests the same +0x128 dword.

arguments.note: Second count t. The routine multiplies it as an unsigned value.

rows.behavior: Reads one int as an unsigned 32 bit second count t and pushes four ints: month ((t / 134400) % 12) + 1, day ((t / 4200) % 32) + 1, hour ((t * 24) / 4200) % 24 and minute ((t * 1440) / 4200) % 60. It reads no world state and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 through 0x005819A0 and keeps the dword in ESI. It pushes four ints through 0x00584F70 in the order month, day, hour, minute into the return cell vector at ExecuteParameters +0x1C.

The month is the high dword of t * 0xF9A9342D shifted right by 17, taken modulo 12 with DIV and increased by 1. The day is the same high dword shifted right by 12, masked with 0x1F and increased by 1.

The hour is t * 24 as a 64 bit product through 0x009D5840, divided by 0x1068 through the unsigned 64 bit divide 0x009D5880 and reduced modulo 0x18 through the unsigned 64 bit remainder 0x009D9AB0. The minute is t * 0x5A0, divided by 0x1068 and reduced modulo 0x3C the same way.

The constant 0xF9A9342D with shifts of 12 and 17 after the 32 bit high multiply is the compiler form of an unsigned division. 2^44 / 0xF9A9342D is 4199.9999998606, and an offline check at the multiples of 4200 and 134400 and their neighbors across the 32 bit range found the shifted products equal to t / 4200 and t / 134400.

4200 is 175 * 24, so 1 hour is 175 seconds, 1 day is 4200 seconds and a month of 32 days is 134400 seconds. Reading t as an Earth second count and the result as the in game calendar is INFERRED from the native name. No instruction reads a clock, so the caller supplies t.

arguments.note: Second count t. The routine multiplies it as an unsigned value.

rows.behavior: Reads one int as an unsigned 32 bit second count t and pushes one int: (((t / 4200) & 0x1F) + 4) / 4, a value from 1 to 8. It reads no world state and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 through 0x005819A0, multiplies the dword by 0xF9A9342D with an unsigned MUL, shifts the high dword right by 12, masks it with 0x1F, adds 4, shifts right by 2 and pushes the result through 0x00584F70.
The masked day index runs 0 to 31, so the pushed value runs 1 to 8 and changes every 4 days.
The value is a moon phase number, by the native name. The names of the phases and the callers that map them to presentation were not traced.

arguments.note: Second count t. The routine multiplies it as an unsigned value.

rows.behavior: Reads one int as an unsigned 32 bit second count t and pushes one int: ((t * 24) / 4200) % 24, the hour from 0 to 23. It reads no world state and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 through 0x005819A0, multiplies the dword by 0x18 with an unsigned MUL, divides the 64 bit product by 0x1068 through 0x009D5880, reduces it modulo 0x18 through 0x009D9AB0 and pushes the low dword through 0x00584F70.

facts.claim: The registrar builds the return list 0x0072BD30, a list of two entries (registry entry 3, the Utf8String, then entry 0, the int), and the empty argument list 0x0072B440. Its one rel32 caller is the call at 0x00754E84 in the PrivateAreaBase switchboard 0x00754E70 (vftable 0x00FD653C slot 2), so the native has order 1.
The callback pushes the address receiver +0xBC through the Utf8String pusher 0x007487C0, then loads the dword at +0x110, adds 1 and pushes it through 0x00584F70.

The switchboard 0x00754E70 has the skip byte shape of the SpreadSheet contracts. It reads the byte at its argument +0x0E. A nonzero byte adds 1 to the word at +0x0C and returns without registering. A zero byte calls the registrar 0x00753A40. It holds no other registrar call.
The string is an area type name and the int an index or ordinal, by the native name and the neighboring AreaBase fields (_isInn reads +0xBA). Their writers and the values they take were not traced.

ledgerCandidates.note: These are the rows of the unimplemented ledger that this record gives a registration, argument list, return list, receiver check and callback contract. A client that implements them still needs the fade consumer behind scene packet type 0x15, the consumers of the weather scene packet types 0x21 and 0x87, the object behind V +0x4E0, the notice queue behind MyPlayer +0xF8 and the writers of the MyPlayer fields at +0x161, +0x165 and +0x166.

boundaries: These are static client observations. No live Lua call or retail-client walk was performed.
Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The run-time order of registration is the switchboard order.
Script call-site counts are static presence in the shipped scripts. They do not establish which natives a given script reaches at run time.

The PlayerBase natives are thunks through the receiver vftable. The behavior recorded for them belongs to the MyPlayer override. A PlayerBase receiver that is not a MyPlayer takes the empty base routine.
The calendar arithmetic is a client computation of a caller supplied integer. Which clock value a script passes to the three Hydaelyn natives was not traced.
The object behind V +0x4E0, the notice queue behind MyPlayer +0xF8, the 0x004D6FE0 call chain and the consumers of every scene record these natives send were not traced.
_setMusic stops at the call of 0x004BBB30. Its behavior is recorded in xivl-decomp:docs/resource/music-song-table.md.
The yield request 0x00CD2860 of _waitForMapLoaded was recorded as a call. Whether it polls the checker once before it suspends was not traced.
